mentl/14ef205:
M4 (the UZero abandon cut) is a distinct Abandon resume-discipline, not the
classifier gate it first looked like. The return-type gate is correct and
stashed: an arm that never resumes only needs to abandon when it returns a
meaningful value, so the UZero grade joins with the op's return type — a bare
type variable (fail's polymorphic bottom) or the never type stay OneShot, and
the three wheel UZero arms are all bottom-typed, so the wheel compiles
byte-identically. But flipping a concrete-return abort to MultiShot traps: the
abort sits in an if-branch, off the k2 spine, so the floor guard rejects it.
Abandon and resume need different lowering (a dead continuation deadens and
unwinds from any position; a live one off-spine cannot be reified), so the
discipline has to carry the distinction. The unwind rides the existing k2
call-boundary propagation, and only the aborting frame needs to deaden its
remainder so post-abort effectful code does not run. The ~15-site cut and the
gates are banked in the design doc; the tree stays at the green fixpoint.

Method note: the UZero census is a static brace-depth scan over the handler
decls, three arms in seconds, not the instrument rebuild this session spent
eighteen minutes on and which never compiled the probe into the compiler.

reserved corner (southpaw-mirrored): first tap arms SURE?, second within

wraps unbounded Text2d at awkward widths — STAG WINS split mid-phrase),
the summoning overlay stands down at MatchOver instead of stacking into

the desktop legend stops clipping off narrow windows.

chain: resimulated ticks overwrite their tape slot, so the tape
converges to confirmed inputs exactly as the game state does and no

ring once per render frame and poisoned the whole tape on any 133ms

shell that was meant to add `import { imageFor, imageStats, WIDTHS }` and the
